text:
alex.k: FYI — Jordan from Acme reported duplicated final generations and unexpected billing spikes after intermittent SSE disconnects. They sent a timeline and logs, looks like reconnect+retry behavior is triggering re-runs.

jordan_customer: Hey team — we saw ~6x extra completions billed for long-running streams. Our UX shows duplicate final paragraphs after the page auto-reconnects. We've reproduced locally by toggling network. Using web SDK v0.9.2 in Chrome.

maria_s: can you paste the exact SDK config + headers you use? specifically idempotency/session token bits.

jordan_customer: we pass:

```json
{
  "stream": true,
  "resume": true,
  "session_token": "acct-xyz",
  "idempotency_key": null
}
```

No explicit idempotency on our side. We rely on SDK resume semantics.

sam_ops: quick thought — if resume attempts replay the final generation chance without proper dedupe semantics, that could double-charge. Need logs showing server resume offset/seq.

alex.k: Jordan attached server-side traces: on disconnect we see resume token `sess:abc:seq:42`, client reconnects and requests resume at 42, then server returns the remainder plus sometimes generates a new completion for the same request id. Paste of trimmed trace below: 

```
[2026-03-08T14:12:03Z] SSE connection open id=conn-11
[2026-03-08T14:12:17Z] stream chunk seq=40 token=tok-A
[2026-03-08T14:12:20Z] connection lost (network)
[2026-03-08T14:12:25Z] reconnect attempt by client with resume_token=sess:abc:seq:42
[2026-03-08T14:12:25Z] server resume accepted, replaying seq>=42
[2026-03-08T14:12:26Z] server generates new completion for request req-789 (unexpected)
[2026-03-08T14:12:27Z] server sends chunk seq=42 token=tok-B
```

maria_s: that line "server generates new completion" is the key. We need to know why the server treats resume as a new inference. Could be session token rotation or request-id mismatch.

sam_ops: also seeing billing incr — the billing backend counts completion creation events rather than chunks sent. If resume triggers completion generation path twice, that explains the extra charges.

alex.k: Jordan — quick repro steps for us to run? They sent a short repro we can run in node.

jordan_customer: repro: start a stream with `max_tokens: 2048` and `stream:true`. After ~midpoint, toggle chrome offline and back online quickly (~5s). You should see duplicated ending paragraphs in 30% of runs. We added a small script:

```bash
# reproduce.sh
node reproduce.js --sdk-version 0.9.2 --stress 50
```

And reproduce.js logs: `resumed at seq 42` then `new completion created req-789`

sam_ops: okay assigning — I'll instrument the resume codepath and add additional debug flags to correlate request-id, resume token and completion-id. Need to know if this is an SDK bug or server-side double-generation.

maria_s: Sarah on runtime mentioned a race where resume path could fall through to full request execution if the finalization flag isn't set on the in-flight generation. That would cause a brand-new generation to run and then the resume replay to send the final chunks as well.

alex.k: for immediate customer mitigation, can they disable automatic resume in the browser? Jordan, can you try `resume:false` in SDK and set client-side reconnect to re-open a fresh session but with `idempotency_key` set to a permanent value per user action — then handle dedupe client-side by ignoring repeated completions with same content hash.

jordan_customer: we can try but disabling resume loses continuity for our users. they prefer resume. Any server-side quick patch?

sam_ops: short-term server mitigations: 1) ensure resume path checks a "finalized" marker to avoid spawning a new generation when there's an in-progress completion; 2) dedupe generation issuance using request-id + session_token + seq; 3) billing: modify counting to attribute to initial generation if resume replay occurs within short window. Those will take work.

maria_s: can you add a temporary heuristic: if resume token seq <= last_seen_seq_for_session AND a completion exists with same request-id, return stored chunks instead of triggering new generation. Low-risk change.

sam_ops: yes, I can prototype that in the resume handler today. Will add logs: `resume-dedup-check session=sess:abc seq=42 match=true`.

alex.k: also need SRE to check network middleboxes — if the client reconnects but server didn't mark previous connection closed, we might end up with two active handles. @sam_ops can you check whether conn-11 was properly tombstoned?

sam_ops: checking, conn-11 shows FIN from client at 14:12:20 but we saw stray keepalive for 1s. possible TCP race on load balancer. I've opened a ticket with infra for sticky-connections and NAT timeout tuning.

support-bot: Ticket created: CS-2147 (escalation: streaming reconnect duplicates & billing) — assigned to sam_ops, priority: high.

maria_s: reproduce plan for tomorrow: run customer repro under proxy that simulates abrupt TCP close (tcpkill) and measure frequency. I'll also write an integration test to mis-order resume vs finalize in the runtime to catch the race.

alex.k: Jordan — for now please set `sdk.resume=false` as a temporary workaround and set `idempotency_key` per user action. We'll follow up with a fix and ETA. Sorry for the UX trouble :(. :handshake:

jordan_customer: thanks, we'll test that now and report back. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

sam_ops: ETA for server-side PR: initial guardrail by EOD tomorrow, full audit next week. Will post PR link when ready.

maria_s: logging action items:
- add resume-dedup check on server (sam_ops)
- adjust billing attribution to avoid double-counting on resume (billing-team follow-up)
- integration test to simulate mid-stream disconnect (maria_s)
- infra NAT/timeout review (infra team)

alex.k: noted. I'll keep CS looped in. If anyone finds the exact code path that spawns new completion, paste snippet here.

support-bot: CS-2147 updated: sam_ops added logs and started a dev instance with resume-dedupe=true for testing.

jordan_customer: quick update: after disabling resume we did one test and duplicates stopped. Re-enabling later to confirm. Thank you all. :pray:
